problem_type: Replace with the reusable failure class
symptom: Replace with the exact user-visible or CI-visible failure
direct_cause: Replace with the observed failure mechanism
class_root: Replace with the shared missing invariant
affected_population: Replace with affected users, inputs, versions, or platforms
entry_points: Replace with a human-readable entry-point summary
internal_only_reason: Replace when official docs or source code cannot decide this internal invariant; otherwise remove this field and add checked external_sources objects.
invariants: Replace with a structural condition that must remain true
generality_proof: Explain why enforcing the declared shared boundaries prevents the same class across every checked entry point.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Explain the invariant owned by this boundary.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Explain how repository evidence ties this entry to the shared boundary.
Explain why this equivalent-looking entry is outside the failure class.

recurrence.reason: Explain why the same mechanism can affect another user, input, entry point, machine, or future run.
same_class_scan: List concrete repository searches and independently checked entry points.

prevention.invariant: State the condition enforced for every caller.
prevention.failure_mode: State how invalid input or state fails closed.
prevention.strategy: Explain how the earliest shared boundary prevents recurrence.

legacy_paths.rationale: Explain why there is no obsolete path, or use status removed and list every changed path that removes old behavior.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Explain why no third-party dependency controls the invariant, or choose upgrade-now/retain-with-exit and fill current, target, and exit_criteria.

migration: Explain how old data, state, scripts, or callers transition; state why no migration is needed when applicable.
residual_risks: List every boundary that remains unproven; do not claim completion for it.
